pages.text: $(bold)The Wizard Armor pattern$()$(br2)is the 16×16 transparent PNG on the left.$(br2)The pattern is only the $(bold)icon on the station layout$() — it has nothing to do with how the armor renders. The armor's real textures live under $(*textures/armor/wizard/$() (greyscale bases tinted per-slot material).

$(bold)Path$(): $(italic)assets/tinkersnewlife/textures/gui/tinker_pattern/wizard_armor.png$()$(br2)Tinkers' $(italic)Pattern.getTexture()$() simply builds $(italic)<namespace>:gui/tinker_pattern/<path>$(), so $(bold)making your own pattern means drawing one 16×16 PNG$() — no models or material rendering involved.$(br2)$(bold)Shared by all four pieces$(): hat / robe / leggings / boots are all selected with this same pattern at the Tinkers' Anvil.

$(bold)How to use it$(): when you pick $(l:tools)Wizard Armor$() at the $(bold)Tinkers' Anvil$(), the station layout shows four slots — $(bold)plating + maille (and $(l:part_robe_lace)robe lace$()) + magic cloth$(); place the materials in the slots to assemble that piece.$(br2)The armor value comes from the material in the $(bold)plating slot$(), while the other parts add durability and their own armor traits, so $(bold)every piece can mix materials$().
